content:
The authorized history purge (owner timing choice: after T-009 lands) ran 2026-08-02, immediately after T-009 closed.

What was rewritten: every blob in history matching the privacy scanner's six personal-value classes (email, macos/linux home account, mangled project dir, session UUID, workflow id) was replaced with the documented synthetic allowlist values, via git-filter-repo regex rules that reproduce the scanner's own token boundaries. 17 rules, 675 replacements across 361 blob instances in 32 dirty commits. Findings from a first literal-rule attempt: a placeholder-truncation artifact would have corrupted synthetic fixture names at HEAD — caught by the tree-identity invariant before any push; the regex rules fixed it.

Verified before push: 85 -> 85 commits; HEAD trees byte-identical on both branches and the tag (zero diff); privacy scanner clean on ALL 85 rewritten commits; zero Claude/Anthropic trailers anywhere.

SHA map (old -> new):
- main: 20ac972 -> b2b09b5
- v0.1-ts-port: 0d15ed3 -> 60cf3d1
- tag v0.1.0: f40cdca -> 17d5b2a (target 4957fbf -> corresponding rewritten commit)
Full 85-line commit map and a pre-purge bundle of the old history are in ~/spendbar-purge-backup/ (owner's machine only — the bundle contains the pre-rewrite values and must never be pushed).

Caveats on the public side: GitHub may keep pre-rewrite objects fetchable by SHA until garbage collection; the owner can ask GitHub Support to drop cached objects for a hard cutoff. Any external clone made before today retains old history. The published npm tarball (0.1.0) was audited clean before release and is unaffected.

Sessions: any tool or agent holding pre-purge SHAs must re-clone or hard-reset to origin. The local repo's branches, tag, and remote-tracking refs are already reset. Stale local-only leftovers referencing old history (stash entries, the worktree-agent branch, refine-codex-dates-combined-view) are inert and local.
title: History purge executed 2026-08-02 — SHA map and provenance
